source.title: On random kernels of residual architectures
source.authors: Etai Littwin; Tomer Galanti; L. Wolf

record.file_problem: Full paper text and appendix are present; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests initialization-time NTK variance and kernel-regression performance for vanilla, residual, and dense architectures. These results bear on whether architecture and depth change training-related behavior, but it does not measure classification training error under the recipes in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports initialization-time normalized NTK variance and accuracy of kernel regression over random gradient features; it does not report gradient-trained classification error. Cited results from other work and values used only as derivation inputs are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures initialization-time NTK statistics and test accuracy from closed-form kernel regression using frozen random gradient features. These do not measure training error, optimization speed, trainable depth, local minima, learning-rate stability, or batch-normalization benefits named in V1–V6. Its own results therefore test none of the listed versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors derive finite-width/depth NTK corrections and argue that appropriately scaled residual architectures are closer to the kernel regime at initialization than vanilla networks, with favorable deep random-gradient-feature kernel-regression results. ResNet guarantees depend on residual scaling; the stated DenseNet convergence bound is independent of depth and initialization scale. These results do not demonstrate gradient-training performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures NTK statistics at random initialization and evaluates kernel regression using random gradient features; it does not train classifiers by gradient descent or report training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture, depth, width, residual scaling, and the number of sampled gradient features T are varied. The initialization-time NTK variance grows with depth for vanilla networks but is relatively constant for ResNets and DenseNets.

fits_no_version.finding: At width 500, normalized NTK variance grows exponentially with depth for vanilla architectures but remains relatively constant for residual and dense architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the tested initialization and scaling, residual and dense architectures have more depth-stable initialization-time NTK variance than vanilla architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing depth harms fixed-width vanilla random-gradient-feature kernel regression on MNIST and UCI, while residual and dense architectures avoid the reported degradation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual and dense architectures preserve random-gradient-feature kernel-regression accuracy with increasing depth better than vanilla architectures in the tested settings.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence
record.problems: The experiment descriptions provide no exact numeric values for the plotted trends in the main text. The MNIST width assignments for Figure 4's second row are inconsistent between caption and prose. The work evaluates random-feature kernel regression and initialization-time NTK statistics, not the classification training-error behavior in the listed versions.

untested.parts: Gradient-trained convolutional-network training classification error, including CIFAR datasets, corrupted labels, model size, stopping time, and regularization.
Teacher-student optimization, spurious local minima, and the benefit of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and training very deep networks with special initialization.
Initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth, including activation matching, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and deep convolutional training.
Loss recovery, curvature evolution, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence under different learning rates.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's comparable training performance without normalization.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6. All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V6; this does not dispute the reported NTK or kernel-regression findings. Figure 3 also reports convolutional NTK statistics, and Figure 5 reports width effects on kernel-regression accuracy, but neither supplies a missing test of a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Training error from random initialization, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, model size, training duration, optimizer, and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Training error of plain versus residual networks and shortcut effects; no classification training-error comparison.
Comparisons of initialization schemes for learning speed or trainable depth; sampled Gaussian initialization is used but its learning consequences are not measured.
Learning-rate stability, loss recovery, sharpness, or divergence during training.
Batch normalization's effect on speed or learning-rate tolerance; no normalized-versus-unnormalized training comparison.
